memo.verdict: Park. Neutral on the stock, bullish on the business; conviction medium. JCDecaux (DEC-FR) at EUR 24.40 (2026-10-05) is a good business at the wrong price: the change forces (B) and the financial outputs (B) are material and have propagated through the whole 'Six Layer Inputs-outputs' chain, but the 'Modal return' is D, about 11.4 percent a year over eighteen months and 10.3 percent a year over three years against the 20 percent bar, because the 24-month-forward multiple of 14.5x already sits at the stock's five-year median and the 90th percentile of the last two years. The park rule by gate is not triggered (management B, business quality B, predictability B, trackability C); the case parks on price. Re-look triggers: a price at or below about EUR 21.8 with our path intact; Q3 2026 trading (late October 2026) with Street Furniture above 5 percent and an H2 2026 operating margin rate not below 24.5 percent; new mid-term targets at the FY2026 results on 2027-03-11. Invalidate: Q3 2026 organic growth below 3.5 percent; FY2026 free cash flow below EUR 280m; the loss of two incumbent street furniture renewals in 2027; FY2026 operating margin rate below 21.0 percent on the company's basis; price above about EUR 26 with our path unchanged.
case: The case is 'Compounder'-type in a cyclical business: a proven under-promiser converting a physical advertising network into a digitally traded one, with the mix shift lifting yield and the cost base growing slower than revenue.

The change is mostly external and a tailwind. Advertising budgets are shifting structurally to digital out-of-home (digital +14.5 percent organic in H1 2026 against +5.7 percent for the group; 42.8 percent of revenue from 36.8 percent; programmatic +30.9 percent to EUR 102.8m at a 25 to 30 percent CPM premium; worldwide out-of-home forecast at +5.2 percent a year to 2030 and digital at +8.8 percent). Competition eased after Clear Channel's acquisition by Mubadala at 12.3x EBITDA removed the loss-tolerant bidder; JCDecaux won 82 percent of the street furniture tenders it contested in 2025 against a sector base rate of about 50 to 60 percent. Disruption (programmatic, retail media, cookie deprecation, AI content) works for physical screens. The supply side is contained: rents and fees +3.4 percent against revenue +5.7 percent, 75 to 80 percent of Chinese transit contracts moved to variable revenue-sharing. The company's own cycle turned up (+5.7 percent organic after +1.8 percent in FY2025; Q3 guided about +5.0 percent). Headwinds are real and smaller: China transit soft with "no major cyclical inflection visible", France minus 1.9 percent, category bans, the French surcharge to 2026, translation currency (EUR 88.4m off FY2025 revenue). Regulation cuts both ways: ESG criteria in over 60 percent of tenders favour the incumbent. External forces B.

The internal change is evolution done well, not a break: strategy shifted toward adtech control (VIOOH EBIT-positive and cash-positive for the first time in H1 2026) and retail media (Carrefour, Carmila, Unlimitail: 161 malls, 297 access points, 900 screens); perimeter pruned (APG|SGA sold down from 16.44 to 5.59 percent at above 13x EBITDA for CHF 71.6m, EUR 79m; French billboard faces halved over a decade); standards tight (fixed costs +0.9 percent, headcount minus 1 percent in 2025, capex capped at 8 percent of sales); price rises real on digital (4x to 5x per-panel uplift) and nominal on traditional inventory (1 to 2 percent a year); shareholder returns resumed (dividend EUR 0.55 then EUR 0.65; small buybacks). No chief executive change (D, the absence of the force), no new mid-term targets (C), bolt-on M&A only, a de-geared rather than used balance sheet. Internal forces C; the screen's rule met at the margin.
counter_case: The bull's case, at full force, and it is the strongest argument in the record. The H1 2026 print changed the narrative from recovery to structural margin expansion. Margins can go on rising toward the 25 percent historical peak as digital goes from 42.8 percent of revenue to 50 percent-plus and programmatic from 12.3 percent of digital toward 20 percent; rents keep lagging revenue because the Chinese and renewed contracts are variable; VIOOH is now self-funding; China is a free option worth about 13 percent on FY2027 EPS (the sell-side's bull case of EUR 1.85 against our EUR 1.64), and Transport's margin recovering toward 20 percent with China would add about EUR 90m, 11 percent of group operating profit, which we count at nothing; the balance sheet at 0.7x can fund bolt-ons at 6x to 7x EBITDA with proceeds raised at 13x; and the stock trades at 7.6x 2026E EV/EBITDA against a ten-year average of 9.0x and at the 29th percentile of its ten-year P/E history, so on an enterprise-value footing it is below its own average. On that reading the multiple goes to the ten-year median of 17.8x and the eighteen-month return is 27.3 percent a year, an A. The upgrade cycle the record itself calls probable has months to run; the two prints ahead are more likely to beat than to miss; the downside is cushioned by a 2.9 percent yield covered nearly three times by free cash flow and by 0.7x leverage; technical momentum is A, sell-side momentum B, relative strength at the 92nd percentile: the market is confirming the thesis. Waiting for EUR 21.8 means waiting for a de-rating the record puts at a quarter's odds while forgoing the beats it expects. And if the Transport or China line moves, consensus is mis-modelled by a step, not a few percent, and the 'Compounder' fit is crisp.

Against the 'Foundations', the bear's structural argument: the moat is the grantor's, not the company's. Every advantage is leased on a contract that comes back to tender; grantors increasingly demand digital conversion as a pre-condition and shorter terms (Paris shortened a concession to five years and took panel ownership; Portuguese municipalities prioritise cash bids); the return on capital employed is capped near 7 percent by the leases whatever the margin does; so the digital yield accrues to the grantor at the next renewal and the H1 2026 margin is a lull between tender rounds.
triggers: - Price: at or below about EUR 21.8 with our path intact, the case re-opens (the eighteen-month bar price; about EUR 19.0 on the three-year horizon). Above about EUR 26 with our path unchanged (three-year return below 8 percent a year), invalidate on the 'Modal return'. Alarm on the multiple: 24-month-forward P/E above 17x without an upgrade cycle to match.

- Q3 2026 trading (late October 2026): Alarm if organic growth is below 4.0 percent or Street Furniture below 4 percent; Invalidate if organic growth is below 3.5 percent; re-look positive if Street Furniture is above 5 percent with an H2 2026 margin not below 24.5 percent (H2 2025 was 25.0 percent). Transport above 3 percent is the review's own test.

- The margin path: our side is probable (about 0.6) that the H2 2026 start-up dilution is temporary and the rate rises 40 to 80 bps a year to 22.6 percent by FY2028; what changes our mind is an H2 2026 operating margin rate below 24.5 percent or an FY2026 rate below 21.0 percent on the company's basis. Watch rents and fees against revenue (Alarm if rents grow faster than revenue in a half) and the rent ratio (about 49 percent).

- FY2026 results (2027-03-11): free cash flow below EUR 280m invalidates; new mid-term targets that lift consensus EPS by 10 percent or more again, or a visible rise in return on capital, would move our side on the multiple toward the re-rating branch.

- The European advertising cycle: a downturn cutting organic growth below 3 percent is possible (about 0.25), not probable; watch the agencies in the comparison set (WPP buy share 18 percent; Havas revision score 1) and a sharp European consumer print as read-across.

- China and Hong Kong transit: a mid-single-digit inflection is plausible (about 0.3) within three years and counted at nothing; two consecutive quarters of mid-single-digit organic growth in Mainland China would make the China line a named consensus error and move the 'Compounder' fit to B.
